cards.title: HELLO, I AM
cards.quote: A khachkar is an Armenian cross-stone. At first, it looks like a carved stone with a cross. But in Armenia, it is much more than decoration — it is memory, prayer, and identity shaped by hand.
cards.label: AM CULTURE

cards.title: HELLO, I AM
cards.quote: The word khachkar literally means "cross-stone": khach means cross, and kar means stone. Most khachkars are vertical stone slabs with a cross at the centre and detailed ornaments around it.
cards.label: AM CULTURE

cards.title: HELLO, I AM
cards.quote: No two khachkars are exactly the same. The patterns can include vines, leaves, circles, rosettes, and lace-like stone carving. Each one carries the hand of the master who made it.
cards.label: AM CULTURE

cards.title: HELLO, I AM
cards.quote: Khachkars can be found near churches, monasteries, cemeteries, roads, and old settlements. Some mark memory. Some mark gratitude. Some simply stand as signs of Armenian presence.
cards.label: AM CULTURE

cards.title: HELLO, I AM
cards.quote: In 2010, Armenian khachkar art was inscribed by UNESCO as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. It is not only a stone object — it is a living craft and a cultural language.
cards.label: AM CULTURE
